person_made_it: In the fallback, yes. Someone decided a no-script reader gets all fifteen slides in order with their text, rather than a polite apology line, and wrote the reason into the generator so the next edition cannot quietly drop it. The page's own look is not mine; I inherited it and left it alone on purpose.
emcee_who_is_speaking: Sinjin is, and that was already right. The gratitude eyebrow names Claire, Lucas and Bigglesworth before any GGP claim, and the headline is what his relationships make possible, not what GGP needs. My addition stays out of the way and does not start a second voice.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Late morning over coffee, warm cream and paper, unhurried. The static deck holds that exact register because a fallback in a different palette would read as the emergency version of the page rather than the page.
did_the_click_pay_me: With script on, yes: arrows, keyboard, full screen, per-slide comment. With script off there is no click to pay, so I removed the ones that lied. Dead prev and next buttons and a select that does nothing are worse than no controls, and both PDF links now actually resolve instead of pointing at the current page.
works_for_the_recipient: This is the whole commit. Sinjin's normal browser was always fine; the failure was anyone reading with script off or blocked, who got a header, a broken image and 1,212 characters. Now 6,597 characters, all 9 slides present, 11 images, 0 broken, no overflow at 390 or 1440, JS-on measured unchanged.
taught_me_something: It taught me that a git checkout is never evidence about production. I read a stale working tree at 10:17 and told Gordon the live page contradicted an email sent to Sinjin. It did not; Astra had already pushed the fix. For a claim about what someone can see right now, the live URL is the only source.
told_me_the_truth: Yes, and it survived a rebuild onto Astra's cleanup. This page is now the 9-slide Scholars deck with Take-Two and every dollar figure removed at Gordon's instruction, and I verified my regenerate reintroduced neither: 0 Take-Two hits, 0 dollar figures, 9 slide images. The only strings my build drops are 'Loading the latest presentation' and 'Latest edition', which it replaces with the real summary and edition date.
weakest: Question 1. The page's visual identity is inherited, and I made a deliberate choice not to touch it mid-presentation, so nothing here answers Gordon's repetitiveness complaint. If this page gets a real design pass later, slide 10 is the tell: 50 lines of text sitting inside an image, which no fallback can make readable at 390.
